options.feedback: Correct! Covering the fire cuts off the oxygen and puts it out safely.

options.text: I would run out of the house.
options.feedback: While you should get to safety, the first step is to try to put out a small fire safely if you can.

questions.question: What would you do if you were cooking with oil and the oil caught fire?
questions.explanation: It's important to know the correct safety procedure for different types of fires. Never use water on an oil fire.

options.text: I would jump in the water to save them.
options.feedback: This can be very dangerous unless you are a trained lifeguard. The drowning person might pull you under.

options.text: I would shout for help and try to throw them something that floats.
options.feedback: Correct. This is the safest way to help. Get the attention of others and provide a flotation device.
You should always try to help in a safe way.

questions.question: What would you do if you saw somebody drowning?
questions.explanation: The safety rule is 'Reach, Throw, Row, Go'. Try to help from a safe distance before entering the water yourself.

activities.title: Mountain Rescue
activities.instruction: You are walking in the mountains when your friend falls and breaks a leg. Make the best choices to handle the situation. This is based on the scenario on PB6.
activities.compensates: Role-playing the mountain scenario in pairs or small groups.

turns.text: What is the first thing you would do?
turns.speaker: system

studentOptions.text: I would try to support his leg.
I would make a fire immediately.
I would run to the village for help.

turns.text: Good choice. You find some wood and use the bandages to make a splint for his leg. He feels a bit better. Now what would you do?
turns.speaker: system

studentOptions.text: I would make a fire to keep him warm and signal for help.
I would leave him and run to the village.

turns.text: Making a fire is a good idea, but it's more important to help your friend directly first. What should you do for his leg?
turns.speaker: system

studentOptions.text: I would use wood and bandages to support it.

turns.text: Leaving your friend alone when he is injured is risky. It's better to make him comfortable and signal for help first. What would you do instead?
turns.speaker: system

studentOptions.text: I would support his leg first.

turns.text: Excellent. You make a fire. The smoke rises high in the air. Soon, you see people from the village coming to help. You both are safe. Well done!
turns.speaker: system

content.scenario: Your friend is on the ground, in pain. 'I think my leg is broken!' he says. You are 2km from the nearest village. You have a warm jacket, bandages, and matches.

activities.title: Pronunciation: 'd Contractions
activities.instruction: Listen carefully! 🎧 Clear your ears and to the full form and the contracted form. Record yourself saying the contracted form and compare it to the original.
activities.compensates: Teacher-led pronunciation drills and repetition.

activities.title: Reflexive Pronouns
activities.instruction: Learn the reflexive pronouns. These are used when the subject and the object of a verb are the same person or thing.
activities.compensates: Vocabulary presentation by the teacher.

cards.example: I can't lift this table by myself.
cards.definition: Used by a speaker to refer to himself or herself as the object of a verb or preposition.

cards.example: Don't swallow those pills! You'll poison yourself.
cards.definition: Used to refer to the person being addressed as the object of a verb or preposition (singular).

cards.example: He taught himself to play the guitar.
cards.definition: Used to refer to a male person as the object of a verb or preposition.

cards.example: Noura hurt herself when she fell down the stairs.
cards.definition: Used to refer to a female person as the object of a verb or preposition.

cards.example: The cat is washing itself.
cards.definition: Used to refer to a thing or animal as the object of a verb or preposition.

cards.example: We should be proud of ourselves for finishing the project.
cards.definition: Used by a speaker to refer to a group including himself or herself as the object of a verb or preposition.

cards.example: You can do these exercises by yourselves.
cards.definition: Used to refer to the people being addressed as the object of a verb or preposition (plural).

cards.example: The boys took sweaters to keep themselves warm.
cards.definition: Used to refer to a group of people, animals, or things as the object of a verb or preposition.

content.feedback: Well done! You have mastered these new words. 🏮

activities.title: Using Reflexive Pronouns
activities.instruction: Complete the sentences with the correct reflexive pronoun. This is based on Workbook page 12, exercise A.
activities.compensates: This activity replaces the written exercise WB 1.15A, providing instant feedback.

content.feedback: Great effort! You've successfully completed the sentences. Keep it up! 🚀

sentences.text: Don't swallow those pills! You'll poison ___ .
sentences.explanation: We use 'yourself' when the subject 'You' (singular) does an action to 'You'.

sentences.text: The boys took sweaters to the camp to keep ___ warm at night.
sentences.explanation: We use 'themselves' when the subject 'The boys' (they) does an action to 'they'.

sentences.text: I can't lift this table by ___ . Can you help me?
sentences.explanation: We use 'myself' when the subject 'I' does an action to 'I'.

sentences.text: Noura hurt ___ when she fell down the stairs.
sentences.explanation: We use 'herself' when the subject 'Noura' (she) does an action to 'she'.

sentences.text: Listen, everybody. You can do these exercises by ___ . You don't need my help.
sentences.explanation: We use 'yourselves' when the subject 'You' (plural) does an action to 'You'.

activities.title: What Would You Do?
activities.instruction: Read the situation and Challenge yourself! 📝 Select the best option for the correct response using the second conditional (if + past simple, ...would + verb). This is based on Workbook page 12, exercise 1.14.
activities.compensates: This digitizes the oral practice from WB 1.14, providing structured choices and immediate feedback on the correct use of the second conditional.

options.text: I would take the matches away from her.
options.feedback: Correct! This uses the 'would + verb' structure for the second conditional.

options.text: I will take the matches away from her.
options.feedback: Incorrect. This is the first conditional. We need the second conditional for hypothetical situations.

options.text: I take the matches away from her.
options.feedback: Incorrect. This is the zero conditional. We need the second conditional for this hypothetical situation.

questions.question: What would you do if you saw your small sister playing with matches?
questions.explanation: The second conditional is used for unlikely or hypothetical situations. The structure is 'if + past simple, ... would + base verb'.

options.text: I would throw water on it.
options.feedback: This is very dangerous! Throwing water on an oil fire can make it explode.

options.text: I would cover the pan with a lid.
options.feedback: Excellent! Covering the pan removes the oxygen and puts out the fire safely.

options.text: I am covering the pan with a lid.
options.feedback: Incorrect verb tense. Remember the 'would + verb' structure for the result clause.

questions.question: What would you do if you were cooking with oil and the oil caught fire?
questions.explanation: In this hypothetical emergency, the safest action is to cover the pan to cut off oxygen. The correct grammatical structure is 'would cover'.

options.text: I would shout for help immediately.
options.feedback: Correct. This is a safe and helpful action, and it uses the correct conditional form.

options.text: I jump in the water to save them.
options.feedback: This can be very dangerous unless you are a trained lifeguard. Also, the grammar is incorrect for the second conditional.

options.text: I would have shouted for help.
options.feedback: This is the third conditional, used for past regrets. The question is about a present hypothetical situation.

questions.question: What would you do if you saw somebody drowning?
questions.explanation: The correct structure for this hypothetical situation is 'would shout'. Alerting others is the first and most important step.
